newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares seen extending Tuesday's gains.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares seen extending Tuesday's gains.

text.p: Hungarian share prices are expected to head upwards on Wednesday, extending gains posted in Tuesday's bull run, traders said, but added the pace of rise will probably slow down.

"The dollar has eased a little (against the forint), the Dow has recovered, so I'm optimistic for the day after a convincing session on Tuesday," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities. "I expect further gains but in a slower pace than yesterday."

On Tuesday the BUX index rocketed to a second successive record high after firming 1.67 percent to 6,597.28 points, bolstered by the upgrade of Hungary's long-term foreign currency rating to BBB from BBB- by IBCA credit rating agency.
The market also benefited from the Finance Minister's announcement that Hungary's monthly crawling peg devaluator will be reduced to one percent from 1.1 percent from August 15.

On Wednesday oil and gas company MOL and chemicals TVK are expected to lead the upward trend, Forgo said, adding MOL was seen receiving support from a 13.5 percent wholesale gas price increase announced on Monday, while TVK was seen rising on expectations of strong first half earnings.
TVK was also seen underpinned by hopes of an imminent decision by privatisation agency APV Rt to grant the company a payout from privatisation revenues.

However, an APV spokesman told Reuters on Monday the payouts to Hungarian companies from APV was not on the agenda of the board's weekly meeting, but added the agenda might change. APV will hold a news conference at 1300 GMT.
Expectations of first half result reports are seen becoming an increasing important driving factor on the market, traders said.
"I expect an upward trend because of Hungary's upgrade and also because I don't see reasons for a fall," said Szabolcs Gyongyosi of Daewoo Securities.
"In addition, sooner or later market talk on corporate earnings is going to start to drive prices higher," he said. "This is usual four to six weeks before the reporting deadline."
Hungarian companies will have to submit their first half earnings reports to the bourse by August 15.
